user_message: I just got a call from the daycare saying that my baby has another ear infection, and I'm just so overwhelmed. I feel like I'm constantly dropping the ball, like I'm not doing anything right. I'm supposed to be this competent, put-together person, but really I'm just a hot mess. And now I'm going to have to take time off work again, and I'll be stuck at home with a sick baby, feeling guilty and anxious and helpless. I'm just so tired of feeling like I'm failing at everything. I'm a terrible mom, a terrible employee, a terrible person. I don't know how much more of this I can take. I'm just so consumed by these feelings of inadequacy, like I'm drowning in a sea of failure and disappointment. Every day feels like a never-ending struggle to keep my head above water, and I'm starting to lose hope that things will ever get better.

analysis.recommended_focus: building self-compassion and reframing negative self-talk

user_message: I'm just so frustrated and helpless, like I'm stuck in this never-ending cycle of failure and disappointment. Every little thing that goes wrong is just another reminder that I'm not good enough, that I'm just a complete and utter failure as a mom, employee, and person. I don't know how much more of this I can take, the guilt and anxiety and helplessness just consume me. I'm so tired of feeling like I'm drowning in this sea of inadequacy, like I'm just a small boat on a stormy sea, tossed around by the waves of my own inadequacy. I just want to scream and cry and throw my hands up in the air and say, "I give up! I just can't do this anymore!" But I know I can't, I have to keep pretending to be strong, to be in control, to be the perfect mom, employee, and person. But it's all just a lie, a facade, a mask
